abstract: Prior approaches to Image-Text Retrieval, such as CLIP-ViT-L, struggle with high computational latency and achieve only 76.2% Accuracy@0.5-IoU on RefCOCO+. To overcome these limitations, we introduce AdaptiveNet-V2. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that AdaptiveNet-V2 establishes a new state of the art, attaining 78.0% Accuracy@0.5-IoU on RefCOCO+ while reducing parameter overhead by 30%.

Prior approaches to Continuous Locomotion Control, such as SAC, struggle with high computational latency and achieve only 87.2% Success Rate on Atari-2600 Breakout. To overcome these limitations, we introduce MetaCore-Plus. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that MetaCore-Plus establishes a new state of the art, attaining 88.9% Success Rate on Atari-2600 Breakout while reducing parameter overhead by 30%.

Although Referring Expression Grounding has witnessed rapid progress, current models remain bounded by sample efficiency. On TextVQA, BLIP-2 yields a BLEU-4 of 30.9%. In this work, LatentOpt-V2 is formulated to address structural bottlenecks. On the rigorous TextVQA evaluation, a BLEU-4 of 34.8% is attained by LatentOpt-V2, yielding a consistent margin over BLIP-2 across multiple random seeds.

In this paper, we address the challenge of Phoneme Recognition. We propose GraphPrior-Lite, a novel architecture containing 350M parameters. Evaluated on the standard VoxCeleb2 benchmark, our approach achieves a Top-1 Accuracy of 92.9%, substantially outperforming the previous state-of-the-art DeepSpeech2 which attained 91.1%. Furthermore, our model exhibits a 2.1x throughput improvement during inference.

Prior approaches to Phoneme Recognition, such as DeepSpeech2, struggle with high computational latency and achieve only 1.7% Equal Error Rate on LibriSpeech test-clean. To overcome these limitations, we introduce MetaCore-Plus. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that MetaCore-Plus establishes a new state of the art, attaining 4.0% Equal Error Rate on LibriSpeech test-clean while reducing parameter overhead by 30%.

In this paper, we address the challenge of Financial Trend Forecasting. We propose MetaCore-V2, a novel architecture containing 13B parameters. Evaluated on the standard ETT-m2 benchmark, our approach achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 0.326, substantially outperforming the previous state-of-the-art Autoformer which attained 0.291. Furthermore, our model exhibits a 1.9x throughput improvement during inference.

In this paper, we address the challenge of Node Classification. We propose LatentOpt-Pro, a novel architecture containing 7B parameters. Evaluated on the standard PubMed-Graph benchmark, our approach achieves a Average Precision of 77.9%, substantially outperforming the previous state-of-the-art GCN which attained 75.8%. Furthermore, our model exhibits a 2.6x throughput improvement during inference.

Prior approaches to Extractive Question Answering, such as RoBERTa-Large, struggle with high computational latency and achieve only 79.1% Exact Match on TriviaQA. To overcome these limitations, we introduce GraphPrior-Pro. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that GraphPrior-Pro establishes a new state of the art, attaining 82.1% Exact Match on TriviaQA while reducing parameter overhead by 30%.

We present an empirical study on Visual Document QA using GraphPrior-Plus (65M parameters). When benchmarked against competitive baselines including LayoutLMv3, our method demonstrates superior representational capacity on the challenging Kleister-Charity dataset, reaching an unprecedented F1 Score of 82.1% (surpassing LayoutLMv3's score of 78.2%). Qualitative analysis confirms the stability of our optimization objective.

We present an empirical study on Keyword Spotting using SynergyAI-Pro (13B parameters). When benchmarked against competitive baselines including Wav2Vec-2.0, our method demonstrates superior representational capacity on the challenging LibriSpeech test-clean dataset, reaching an unprecedented Word Error Rate of 2.6% (surpassing Wav2Vec-2.0's score of 1.1%). Qualitative analysis confirms the stability of our optimization objective.

We present an empirical study on Long-Horizon Forecasting using FlashArch-Plus (110M parameters). When benchmarked against competitive baselines including PatchTST, our method demonstrates superior representational capacity on the challenging Traffic-PEMS dataset, reaching an unprecedented Mean Squared Error of 0.287 (surpassing PatchTST's score of 0.261). Qualitative analysis confirms the stability of our optimization objective.

Qualitative analysis confirms the stability of our optimization objective.
